\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{قسم} \fa{خوردن} (qasam khordan)}{قسم خوردن (qasam khordan)}]{\fa{قسم} \fa{خوردن} (qasam khordan) — to swear, to take an oath}

\label{lesson:FA-C321-qasam-khordan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a fingerprint, then the Persian for an interrogation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{قسم} \fa{خوردن}}
\textbf{\fa{قسم} \fa{خوردن}} (\emph{qasam khordan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to swear, to take an oath\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{قسم} \fa{خورد} \fa{که} \fa{چیزی} \fa{ندیده} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{U qasam khord ke chizi nadide ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He swore that he had not seen anything.
\end{quote}

Literally \textquotedblleft{}to eat an oath\textquotedblright{}. Present \emph{qasam mikhorad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{qasam} \textquotedblleft{}an oath\textquotedblright{} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{qasam} (EtymDB). \emph{khordan} \textquotedblleft{}to eat\textquotedblright{} is inherited, from Middle Persian \emph{xwar-} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qasam khordan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qasam khordan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{qasam khordan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a fingerprint, then the Persian for an interrogation, then say \emph{qasam khordan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{شهادت} \fa{دادن} (shahâdat dâdan)}{شهادت دادن (shahâdat dâdan)}]{\fa{شهادت} \fa{دادن} (shahâdat dâdan) — to testify, to give evidence}

\label{lesson:FA-C321-shahadat-dadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an interrogation, then the Persian for to swear.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{شهادت} \fa{دادن}}
\textbf{\fa{شهادت} \fa{دادن}} (\emph{shahâdat dâdan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to testify, to give evidence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{همسایه} \fa{به} \fa{نفع} \fa{او} \fa{شهادت} \fa{داد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Hamsâye be naf'-e u shahâdat dâd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The neighbour testified in his favour.
\end{quote}

\emph{shahâdat} \textquotedblleft{}witnessing\textquotedblright{} also means \textquotedblleft{}martyrdom\textquotedblright{} in religious use. Present \emph{shahâdat midahad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{shahâdat} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{shahāda}, \textquotedblleft{}witnessing\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB). \emph{dâdan} \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shahâdat dâdan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shahâdat dâdan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{shahâdat dâdan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for an interrogation, then the Persian for to swear, then say \emph{shahâdat dâdan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{شهادت} \fa{دادن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To testify, to give evidence\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اقرار} \fa{کردن} (eqrâr kardan)}{اقرار کردن (eqrâr kardan)}]{\fa{اقرار} \fa{کردن} (eqrâr kardan) — to admit, to own up}

\label{lesson:FA-C321-eqrar-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to swear, then the Persian for to testify.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اقرار} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{اقرار} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{eqrâr kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to admit, to own up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پسر} \fa{اقرار} \fa{کرد} \fa{که} \fa{پنجره} \fa{را} \fa{شکسته} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Pesar eqrâr kard ke panjere râ shekaste ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The boy admitted that he had broken the window.
\end{quote}

Present \emph{eqrâr mikonad}. Close in meaning to \textquotedblleft{}to confess\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{eqrâr} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{iqrār} (EtymDB lists the Arabic word), usually glossed \textquotedblleft{}acknowledgement\textquotedblright{}. \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{eqrâr kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{eqrâr kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to swear, then the Persian for to testify, then say \emph{eqrâr kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{لو} \fa{دادن} (low dâdan)}{لو دادن (low dâdan)}]{\fa{لو} \fa{دادن} (low dâdan) — to give away, to betray (a secret or a person)}

\label{lesson:FA-C321-low-dadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to testify, then the Persian for to admit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{لو} \fa{دادن}}
\textbf{\fa{لو} \fa{دادن}} (\emph{low dâdan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to give away, to betray (a secret or a person)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دوستش} \fa{او} \fa{را} \fa{لو} \fa{داد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dustash u râ low dâd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
His friend gave him away.
\end{quote}

Colloquial. Present \emph{low midahad}. Compare \emph{low raftan} \textquotedblleft{}to be found out\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dâdan} \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian. The origin of \emph{low} \textquotedblleft{}revealed, exposed\textquotedblright{} is not settled; EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{low dâdan}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to testify, then the Persian for to admit, then say \emph{low dâdan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{گناهکار} (gonâhkâr)}{گناهکار (gonâhkâr)}]{\fa{گناهکار} (gonâhkâr) — guilty; a guilty person}

\label{lesson:FA-C321-gonahkar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to admit, then the Persian for to give away.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{گناهکار}}
\textbf{\fa{گناهکار}} (\emph{gonâhkâr}) — \textquotedblleft{}guilty; a guilty person\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{همه} \fa{فکر} \fa{میکردند} \fa{او} \fa{گناهکار} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Hame fekr mikardand u gonâhkâr ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Everyone thought he was guilty.
\end{quote}

\emph{gonâh} \textquotedblleft{}sin, fault\textquotedblright{} + \emph{-kâr} \textquotedblleft{}doer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gonâhkâr} joins \emph{gonâh} \textquotedblleft{}sin, fault\textquotedblright{} and the suffix \emph{-kâr} \textquotedblleft{}doer\textquotedblright{}, both native Persian. EtymDB lists \emph{gonâh} without a parent.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
